#3 Review of the idea: novelty gap (CAT/MCAT), T1–T3 stated precisely, leakage, matrix definition, scope of generative transfer
State:   open
Author:  idea-review-repo

# Review of the idea (Brief rev. 2026-11-26 21:05; `related_work/*` @1a47993)

Overall: a clear, falsifiable, honest idea with a defensible protocol. It is a good base. The points below are what would stop a reviewer at ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS or make the evidence undecidable; each has a proposed fix. Ordered by importance. Decisions stay yours.

## What is strong
- Question Q is operational (which k, how to infer, how large k) and matches the objective's success measure (closeness of inferred to measured scores on unrun benchmarks).
- Protocol is the right one: whole new model held out, standardisation/factor fit/selection fit on others only; run set limited to benchmarks the model really has; a floor from "all other N−1 given"; bootstrap over models and paired differences.
- Hypotheses H1–H5 are falsifiable, and the Brief states that a negative result (random-k + PPCA matches design beyond small k) is a valid main result. That is the correct attitude; keep it as a pre-registered branch, not a footnote.
- Baseline list separates selection (S) from inference (P). Keep this S×P factorial: it is what lets the paper say *where* a gain comes from.
- Honest about MTEB being embedding models.

## Issues, most important first

**1. Novelty is thinner than the Brief says; the closest prior work is missing.** Selecting a few "items" to measure a latent trait vector and predict the rest is exactly *multidimensional computerized adaptive testing* with A-/D-optimality item selection (e.g. Mulder & van der Linden, "Multidimensional adaptive testing with optimal design criteria for item selection", Psychometrika 2009, doi:10.1007/s11336-008-9097-5, seen in search), and *active learning for cold-start matrix factorisation* (e.g. Houlsby et al., ICML 2014, "Cold-start active learning with robust ordinal matrix factorization", seen in search; Rashid/Golbandi already listed). Positioning cites CAT/IRT in the "caveat on discovery" only. A reviewer from either field will say "this is MCAT with benchmarks as items". Also the MTEB-side question "which k tasks" is very close to LLM-evaluation work on IRT/adaptive testing (e.g. "Lost in Benchmarks?" PSN-IRT, arXiv:2505.15055 — seen in search; check, do not cite unread). Fix: add a CAT/MCAT line to `positioning.md`, state plainly that the machinery is classical and the contribution is (i) the empirical answer on real leaderboards under a held-out-model protocol, (ii) the k*(ε) rule tied to the spectrum, (iii) where theory breaks. Do not sell the *method* as new; sell the *evidence and scope conditions*. Also verify (not just list as TV) Mazumder 2010 and Chaloner–Verdinelli 1995.

**2. T3 (adaptive = batch) is a textbook fact and is oversold.** For linear-Gaussian models with known parameters the posterior covariance does not depend on y, so sequential and batch designs coincide: standard in Bayesian linear design, not a finding "against cold-start wisdom" (recommender adaptivity gains come from misspecification — mixtures, non-Gaussian ratings — and from learning parameters online). Fix: present T3 as a one-paragraph proposition (state assumptions: known V, σ², Gaussian, squared loss, fixed run set), call it a sanity check, and put the weight on the *empirical* question: how much does adaptivity gain on real matrices where the assumptions fail, and why. Make explicit that the S7 tree/kNN interview tests *misspecification*, not T3 (they are different models); the clean T3 test is adaptive vs batch under the *same* PPCA posterior, which should agree to numerical precision on every held-out model (a unit test, not an experiment).

**3. T1/T2 as written are partly tautological and T2's "sharp drop at r" conflicts with "r/k decay".**
- "Matches exactly on synthetic matrices" is only a check of the algebra if synthetic data are drawn f
[truncated for publication]

cd /hutian/wiki && cat > Brief.md <<'EOF'
# Brief — the idea (rev. 2 after idea review #3)

## Task as I read it
A new model can be run on only k of N benchmarks; a historical model × benchmark matrix (cells missing) is available. Choose the k benchmarks and infer the other N−k scores as accurately as possible; say how large k must be, and under which data conditions that holds. Deliverable: a venue-grade paper (ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS) plus code; claims rest on real leaderboard matrices and a theory checked against data.

## Question
**Q.** Given a historical score matrix, which k benchmarks should be run for a new model, how should the rest be inferred, and how large must k be for the error to reach the level the low-rank structure allows? Under which data conditions does the answer hold?

## What the contribution is (and is not)
The machinery is classical: item selection by A-/D-optimal design for a latent trait vector (multidimensional computerized adaptive testing, Mulder & van der Linden 2009), cold-start active learning for matrix factorisation (Rashid 2002, Golbandi 2011, Houlsby 2014), probabilistic PCA, greedy subset selection with submodularity-ratio guarantees. **I do not claim a new selection method.** The contribution is: (i) the empirical answer on real leaderboard matrices under the protocol that matches the use (whole new models held out, by group; selection fit on others only); (ii) a sufficiency rule k*(ε) tied to the spectrum of the matrix, with its misfit term made explicit; (iii) the **scope map**: where the answer holds and where it never reaches the floor (extrapolation to new families/strongest models, sparse coverage, small M, saturated scores, task granularity), including a misspecification ladder on synthetic data on which real matrices are placed.

## Model and selection
- y_{mj} = μ_j + v_jᵀ z_m + ε_{mj}, ε~N(0,σ_j²) on standardised scores, fitted by EM on observed cells (probabilistic PCA/FA with missing data); transform/link as a sensitivity variant.
- New model: posterior of z given the run set S. Selection objective with a **fixed target**: F(S) = tr(V Σ_post(S) Vᵀ) over all benchmarks (or a weighted version / the unrun-only variant; compared empirically). Greedy; the Das–Kempe / Bian et al. guarantee is reported but may be vacuous at low noise, so greedy is checked against exhaustive search (small N) and swap/local search. Posterior covariance is independent of y, so selection is an offline subset problem per run-set restriction. Cost-aware variant (gain per cost, equal-cost random comparator) only if a real cost source exists (MTEB `evaluation_time`, to be confirmed), else dropped or a stated proxy.

## Theory (stated with assumptions; each checked)
- **T1 (risk decomposition).** Under the model with *known* parameters: E err_j(S) = σ_j² + v_jᵀ(I + V_SᵀΣ_S⁻¹V_S)⁻¹v_j. With parameters estimated from M models there is an additional estimation term, predicted to scale ~1/M. Empirical risk(k) = residual floor + design term(k) + misfit(k); the misfit term is reported on real data.
- **T2 (shape of the curve).** Two regimes, stated before results: with separated factors (eigenvalues ≫ σ²) a knee near effective rank r; with decaying spectrum a gradual closure and ~1/k decay whose constant depends on the incoherence of the loadings. Effective rank is defined *before* looking at results (parallel analysis, eigenvalues above the noise edge, CV-selected rank; sensitivity to imputation reported). k*(ε) = smallest k whose predicted design term ≤ ε, in raw score points as well as standardised units.
- **T3 (adaptive = batch)** — a one-paragraph proposition (known V, σ², Gaussian, squared loss, fixed run set; textbook), verified as a unit test under the same posterior. The empirical question is what adaptivity gains where assumptions fail (tree/kNN interviews test misspecification, not T3).
- **T4 (random-k near-optimal beyond r + margin)** — a conjecture supported by simulation; appendix.

cat > /tmp/reply.md <<'EOF'
Brief rev. 2 (wiki 7fd99bc) and `related_work/*` (repo 30cc894) answer this review. Accepted, with where each landed:

1. **Novelty** — accepted. MCAT (Mulder & van der Linden 2009) and cold-start active learning (Houlsby 2014) added as ancestors, both verified; Mazumder 2010 (jmlr.org page) and Chaloner–Verdinelli 1995 (Crossref) verified. The Brief now says "no new selection method"; the contribution is evidence, k*(ε) with misfit, and the scope map. PSN-IRT: only the abstract was read, so it is mentioned as item-level IRT work and not cited.
2. **T3** — accepted: a one-paragraph proposition with assumptions, plus a unit test under the same PPCA posterior. S7 tests misspecification gains.
3. **T1/T2/T4** — accepted: an estimation term ~1/M, risk = floor + design + misfit with the misfit reported, effective rank defined before results, two regimes (knee vs 1/k) with the incoherence dependence, a misspecification ladder on synthetic data; T4 is a conjecture in the appendix.
4. **"Noise floor"** — accepted: renamed "residual floor" and "all-others floor".
5. **Leakage** — accepted: group-wise hold-out is primary, with dedup fixed beforehand; LOMO is a sensitivity check.
6. **Matrix definition** — accepted: one benchmark = one task, main score, one revision per model, a granularity sweep, a coverage table, the MNAR limitation, and the gate (≳100 models × ≳30 tasks, else narrow the claims). The exact cell rule must be written down by `experiment-repo` before running; I do not know the JSON fields well enough to fix them.
7. **Generative transfer** — accepted: scope stated; `open-llm-leaderboard/results` subtasks and LiveBench per-task are the options; N=6 and N=10 are used only for exhaustive-oracle checks. "Embedding models" must appear in the title/abstract unless a generative matrix with N≳20 supports the claim.
8. **Objective** — accepted: fixed-target F(S)=tr(VΣ_post Vᵀ); the unrun-only variant is compared empirically; the guarantee is reported but greedy is checked against exhaustive and swap search; equal-cost comparison for the cost-aware variant, dropped if no real cost source exists.
9. **Metrics** — accepted: raw-point MAE, error vs neighbouring-model gap, strong-model ranking, per-benchmark error.
10. **Equal terms** — accepted: the same inner CV for all; the primary contrast is S6+P5 vs S0+P5 at k∈{1,2,3,5,8,12,20}; gain judged against random-k spread; k=1–3 vs mean-offset reported.
11. **Scope** — accepted: the main line is in the Brief for `story-repo`; the T3/T4 and S×P grid go to the appendix.

Not changed: S×P kept as a factorial, but the primary claim rests on one contrast. Smaller points are all taken. Please re-review the Brief.
EOF

shown.message:
I accepted the idea review (issue #3) and revised the idea. I replied on the issue and closed it. I ran no experiments, so the theory is still unchecked.

- **Contribution:** it is now the evidence and the scope map. The Brief says plainly that I don't claim a new selection method. The machinery is classical: multidimensional adaptive testing (Mulder & van der Linden 2009) and cold-start active learning (Houlsby 2014, Rashid 2002, Golbandi 2011).
- **Theory:** the risk is now written as residual floor + design term + misfit. The adaptive-equals-batch result (T3) is a short proposition checked as a unit test. The random-k-near-optimal claim (T4) is a conjecture for the appendix.
- **Protocol:** the primary hold-out is by model family, with plain leave-one-model-out only as a sensitivity check. The matrix definition and a data gate are pinned, and one primary contrast is fixed in advance: designed selection versus random-k with the same inference. The Brief also adds more metrics and a synthetic misspecification ladder.
- **Scope:** the generative-LLM transfer needs a matrix with about 20 or more benchmarks. Otherwise the title and abstract must say "embedding models".
- **Not settled:** the exact MTEB cell rule must be fixed by `experiment-repo` before any run. I don't know the JSON fields well enough to fix it.
- **References:** Mazumder 2010 and Chaloner–Verdinelli 1995 are now verified, along with the two new ones. I read only the abstract of the PSN-IRT paper, so I left it uncited.

The wiki `Brief` is at 7fd99bc and `related_work/` in the repository is at 30cc894. The review says it will re-review once the Brief changes, and my commitment issue (#2) stays open.
